units.leftText: On many past occasions and in many different ways, God spoke to our fathers through the prophets.
units.rightText: God, having of old time spoken unto the fathers in the prophets by divers portions and in divers manners,

units.leftText: But in these last days He has spoken to us by His Son, whom He appointed heir of all things, and through whom He made the universe.
units.rightText: hath at the end of these days spoken unto us in his Son, whom he appointed heir of all things, through whom also he made the worlds;
leftNotes: 1:2 Or the world; literally the ages

units.leftText: The Son is the radiance of God’s glory and the exact representation of His nature, upholding all things by His powerful word. After He had provided purification for sins, He sat down at the right hand of the Majesty on high.
units.rightText: who being the effulgence of his glory, and the very image of his substance, and upholding all things by the word of his power, when he had made purification of sins, sat down on the right hand of the Majesty on high;

units.leftText: So He became as far superior to the angels as the name He has inherited is excellent beyond theirs.
units.rightText: having become by so much better than the angels, as he hath inherited a more excellent name than they.

units.leftText: For to which of the angels did God ever say: “You are My Son; today I have become Your Father” ? Or again: “I will be His Father, and He will be My Son” ?
units.rightText: For unto which of the angels said he at any time, Thou art my Son, This day have I begotten thee? and again, I will be to him a Father, And he shall be to me a Son?
leftNotes: 1:5 Psalm 2:7|PSA 2:7*; literally today I have begotten You

units.leftText: And again, when God brings His firstborn into the world, He says: “Let all God’s angels worship Him.”
units.rightText: And when he again bringeth in the firstborn into the world he saith, And let all the angels of God worship him.

units.leftText: Now about the angels He says: “He makes His angels winds, His servants flames of fire.”
units.rightText: And of the angels he saith, Who maketh his angels winds, And his ministers a flame of fire:

units.leftText: But about the Son He says: “Your throne, O God, endures forever and ever, and justice is the scepter of Your kingdom.
units.rightText: but of the Son he saith, Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever; And the sceptre of uprightness is the sceptre of thy kingdom.

units.leftText: You have loved righteousness and hated wickedness; therefore God, Your God, has anointed You above Your companions with the oil of joy.”
units.rightText: Thou hast loved righteousness, and hated iniquity; Therefore God, thy God, hath anointed thee With the oil of gladness above thy fellows.

units.leftText: And: “In the beginning, O Lord, You laid the foundations of the earth, and the heavens are the work of Your hands.
units.rightText: And, Thou, Lord, in the beginning didst lay the foundation of the earth, And the heavens are the works of thy hands:

units.leftText: They will perish, but You remain; they will all wear out like a garment.
units.rightText: They shall perish; but thou continuest: And they all shall wax old as doth a garment;

units.leftText: You will roll them up like a robe; like a garment they will be changed; but You remain the same, and Your years will never end.”
units.rightText: And as a mantle shalt thou roll them up, As a garment, and they shall be changed: But thou art the same, And thy years shall not fail.
leftNotes: 1:12 BYZ and TR do not include like a garment.

units.leftText: Yet to which of the angels did God ever say: “Sit at My right hand until I make Your enemies a footstool for Your feet” ?
units.rightText: But of which of the angels hath he said at any time, Sit thou on my right hand, Till I make thine enemies the footstool of thy feet?

units.leftText: Are not the angels ministering spirits sent to serve those who will inherit salvation?
units.rightText: Are they not all ministering spirits, sent forth to do service for the sake of them that shall inherit salvation?

units.leftText: We must pay closer attention, therefore, to what we have heard, so that we do not drift away.
units.rightText: Therefore we ought to give the more earnest heed to the things that were heard, lest haply we drift away from them.

units.leftText: For if the message spoken by angels was binding, and every transgression and disobedience received its just punishment,
units.rightText: For if the word spoken through angels proved stedfast, and every transgression and disobedience received a just recompense of reward;

units.leftText: how shall we escape if we neglect such a great salvation?
units.rightText: how shall we escape, if we neglect so great a salvation? which having at the first been spoken through the Lord, was confirmed unto us by them that heard;

units.leftText: and was affirmed by God through signs, wonders, various miracles, and gifts of the Holy Spirit distributed according to His will. Jesus like His Brothers
units.rightText: God also bearing witness with them, both by signs and wonders, and by manifold powers, and by gifts of the Holy Spirit, according to his own will.

units.leftText: For it is not to angels that He has subjected the world to come, about which we are speaking.
units.rightText: For not unto angels did he subject the world to come, whereof we speak.

units.leftText: But somewhere it is testified in these words: “What is man that You are mindful of him, or the son of man that You care for him?
units.rightText: But one hath somewhere testified, saying, What is man, that thou art mindful of him? Or the son of man, that thou visitest him?

units.leftText: You made him a little lower than the angels; You crowned him with glory and honor
units.rightText: Thou madest him a little lower than the angels; Thou crownedst him with glory and honor, And didst set him over the works of thy hands:
leftNotes: 2:7 Or a little while lower; also in verse 9
2:7 WH and TR include and set him over the works of Your hands.

units.leftText: and placed everything under his feet.”
units.rightText: Thou didst put all things in subjection under his feet. For in that he subjected all things unto him, he left nothing that is not subject to him. But now we see not yet all things subjected to him.

units.leftText: But we see Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels, now crowned with glory and honor because He suffered death, so that by the grace of God He might taste death for everyone.
units.rightText: But we behold him who hath been made a little lower than the angels, even Jesus, because of the suffering of death crowned with glory and honor, that by the grace of God he should taste of death for every man.

units.leftText: In bringing many sons to glory, it was fitting for God, for whom and through whom all things exist, to make the author of their salvation perfect through suffering.
units.rightText: For it became him, for whom are all things, and through whom are all things, in bringing many sons unto glory, to make the author of their salvation perfect through sufferings.

units.leftText: For both the One who sanctifies and those who are sanctified are of the same family. So Jesus is not ashamed to call them brothers.
units.rightText: For both he that sanctifieth and they that are sanctified are all of one: for which cause he is not ashamed to call them brethren,

units.leftText: He says: “I will proclaim Your name to My brothers; I will sing Your praises in the assembly.”
units.rightText: saying, I will declare thy name unto my brethren, In the midst of the congregation will I sing thy praise.

units.leftText: And again: “I will put My trust in Him.” And once again: “Here am I, and the children God has given Me.”
units.rightText: And again, I will put my trust in him. And again, Behold, I and the children whom God hath given me.

units.leftText: Now since the children have flesh and blood, He too shared in their humanity, so that by His death He might destroy him who holds the power of death, that is, the devil,
units.rightText: Since then the children are sharers in flesh and blood, he also himself in like manner partook of the same; that through death he might bring to nought him that had the power of death, that is, the devil;

units.leftText: and free those who all their lives were held in slavery by their fear of death.
units.rightText: and might deliver all them who through fear of death were all their lifetime subject to bondage.

units.leftText: For surely it is not the angels He helps, but the descendants of Abraham.
units.rightText: For verily not to angels doth he give help, but he giveth help to the seed of Abraham.

units.leftText: For this reason He had to be made like His brothers in every way, so that He might become a merciful and faithful high priest in service to God, in order to make atonement for the sins of the people.
units.rightText: Wherefore it behooved him in all things to be made like unto his brethren, that he might become a merciful and faithful high priest in things pertaining to God, to make propitiation for the sins of the people.

units.leftText: Because He Himself suffered when He was tempted, He is able to help those who are being tempted.
units.rightText: For in that he himself hath suffered being tempted, he is able to succor them that are tempted.

units.leftText: Therefore, holy brothers, who share in the heavenly calling, set your focus on Jesus, the apostle and high priest whom we confess.
units.rightText: Wherefore, holy brethren, partakers of a heavenly calling, consider the Apostle and High Priest of our confession, even Jesus;

units.leftText: He was faithful to the One who appointed Him, just as Moses was faithful in all God’s house.
units.rightText: who was faithful to him that appointed him, as also was Moses in all his house.
leftNotes: 3:2 Literally just as Moses in all His house; SBL just as Moses in His house

units.leftText: For Jesus has been counted worthy of greater glory than Moses, just as the builder of a house has greater honor than the house itself.
units.rightText: For he hath been counted worthy of more glory than Moses, by so much as he that built the house hath more honor than the house.

units.leftText: And every house is built by someone, but God is the builder of everything.
units.rightText: For every house is builded by some one; but he that built all things is God.

units.leftText: Now Moses was faithful as a servant in all God’s house, testifying to what would be spoken later.
units.rightText: And Moses indeed was faithful in all his house as a servant, for a testimony of those things which were afterward to be spoken;

units.leftText: But Christ is faithful as the Son over God’s house. And we are His house, if we hold firmly to our confidence and the hope of which we boast. Do Not Harden Your Hearts (Psalm 95:1–11|PSA 95:1-11*)
units.rightText: but Christ as a son, over his house; whose house are we, if we hold fast our boldness and the glorying of our hope firm unto the end.
leftNotes: 3:6 NE, WH, BYZ, and TR include to the end.

units.leftText: Therefore, as the Holy Spirit says: “Today, if you hear His voice,
units.rightText: Wherefore, even as the Holy Spirit saith, To-day if ye shall hear his voice,

units.leftText: do not harden your hearts, as you did in the rebellion, in the day of testing in the wilderness,
units.rightText: Harden not your hearts, as in the provocation, Like as in the day of the trial in the wilderness,

units.leftText: where your fathers tested and tried Me, and for forty years saw My works.
units.rightText: Where your fathers tried me by proving me, And saw my works forty years.

units.leftText: Therefore I was angry with that generation, and I said, ‘Their hearts are always going astray, and they have not known My ways.’
units.rightText: Wherefore I was displeased with this generation, And said, They do always err in their heart: But they did not know my ways;

units.leftText: So I swore on oath in My anger, ‘They shall never enter My rest.’” The Peril of Unbelief
units.rightText: As I sware in my wrath, They shall not enter into my rest.

units.leftText: See to it, brothers, that none of you has a wicked heart of unbelief that turns away from the living God.
units.rightText: Take heed, brethren, lest haply there shall be in any one of you an evil heart of unbelief, in falling away from the living God:

units.leftText: But exhort one another daily, as long as it is called today, so that none of you may be hardened by sin’s deceitfulness.
units.rightText: but exhort one another day by day, so long as it is called To-day; lest any one of you be hardened by the deceitfulness of sin:

units.leftText: We have come to share in Christ if we hold firmly to the end the assurance we had at first.
units.rightText: for we are become partakers of Christ, if we hold fast the beginning of our confidence firm unto the end:

units.leftText: As it has been said: “Today, if you hear His voice, do not harden your hearts, as you did in the rebellion.”
units.rightText: while it is said, To-day if ye shall hear his voice, Harden not your hearts, as in the provocation.

units.leftText: For who were the ones who heard and rebelled? Were they not all those Moses led out of Egypt?
units.rightText: For who, when they heard, did provoke? nay, did not all they that came out of Egypt by Moses?

units.leftText: And with whom was God angry for forty years? Was it not with those who sinned, whose bodies fell in the wilderness?
units.rightText: And with whom was he displeased forty years? was it not with them that sinned, whose bodies fell in the wilderness?

units.leftText: And to whom did He swear that they would never enter His rest? Was it not to those who disobeyed?
units.rightText: And to whom sware he that they should not enter into his rest, but to them that were disobedient?

units.leftText: So we see that it was because of their unbelief that they were unable to enter.
units.rightText: And we see that they were not able to enter in because of unbelief.

units.leftText: Therefore, while the promise of entering His rest still stands, let us be careful that none of you be deemed to have fallen short of it.
units.rightText: Let us fear therefore, lest haply, a promise being left of entering into his rest, any one of you should seem to have come short of it.

units.leftText: For we also received the good news just as they did; but the message they heard was of no value to them, since they did not share the faith of those who comprehended it.
units.rightText: For indeed we have had good tidings preached unto us, even as also they: but the word of hearing did not profit them, because it was not united by faith with them that heard.
leftNotes: 4:2 Literally not having been united in the faith of those who heard

units.leftText: Now we who have believed enter that rest. As for the others, it is just as God has said: “So I swore on oath in My anger, ‘They shall never enter My rest.’”
units.rightText: For we who have believed do enter into that rest; even as he hath said, As I sware in my wrath, They shall not enter into my rest: although the works were finished from the foundation of the world.

units.leftText: For somewhere He has spoken about the seventh day in this manner: “And on the seventh day God rested from all His works.”
units.rightText: For he hath said somewhere of the seventh day on this wise, And God rested on the seventh day from all his works;

units.leftText: And again, as He says in the passage above: “They shall never enter My rest.”
units.rightText: and in this place again, They shall not enter into my rest.

units.leftText: Since, then, it remains for some to enter His rest, and since those who formerly heard the good news did not enter because of their disobedience,
units.rightText: Seeing therefore it remaineth that some should enter thereinto, and they to whom the good tidings were before preached failed to enter in because of disobedience,

units.leftText: God again designated a certain day as “Today,” when a long time later He spoke through David as was just stated: “Today, if you hear His voice, do not harden your hearts.”
units.rightText: he again defineth a certain day, To-day, saying in David so long a time afterward (even as hath been said before), To-day if ye shall hear his voice, Harden not your hearts.

units.leftText: For if Joshua had given them rest, God would not have spoken later about another day.
units.rightText: For if Joshua had given them rest, he would not have spoken afterward of another day.

units.leftText: There remains, then, a Sabbath rest for the people of God.
units.rightText: There remaineth therefore a sabbath rest for the people of God.

units.leftText: For whoever enters God’s rest also rests from his own work, just as God did from His.
units.rightText: For he that is entered into his rest hath himself also rested from his works, as God did from his.

units.leftText: Let us, therefore, make every effort to enter that rest, so that no one will fall by following the same pattern of disobedience. The Living Word (2 Timothy 3:10–17|2TI 3:10-17*)
units.rightText: Let us therefore give diligence to enter into that rest, that no man fall after the same example of disobedience.

units.leftText: For the word of God is living and active. Sharper than any double-edged sword, it pierces even to dividing soul and spirit, joints and marrow. It judges the thoughts and intentions of the heart.
units.rightText: For the word of God is living, and active, and sharper than any two-edged sword, and piercing even to the dividing of soul and spirit, of both joints and marrow, and quick to discern the thoughts and intents of the heart.

units.leftText: Nothing in all creation is hidden from God’s sight; everything is uncovered and exposed before the eyes of Him to whom we must give account.
units.rightText: And there is no creature that is not manifest in his sight: but all things are naked and laid open before the eyes of him with whom we have to do.

units.leftText: Therefore, since we have a great high priest who has passed through the heavens, Jesus the Son of God, let us hold firmly to what we profess.
units.rightText: Having then a great high priest, who hath passed through the heavens, Jesus the Son of God, let us hold fast our confession.

units.leftText: For we do not have a high priest who is unable to sympathize with our weaknesses, but we have one who was tempted in every way that we are, yet was without sin.
units.rightText: For we have not a high priest that cannot be touched with the feeling of our infirmities; but one that hath been in all points tempted like as we are, yet without sin.

units.leftText: Let us then approach the throne of grace with confidence, so that we may receive mercy and find grace to help us in our time of need.
units.rightText: Let us therefore draw near with boldness unto the throne of grace, that we may receive mercy, and may find grace to help us in time of need.

units.leftText: Every high priest is appointed from among men to represent them in matters relating to God, to offer gifts and sacrifices for sins.
units.rightText: For every high priest, being taken from among men, is appointed for men in things pertaining to God, that he may offer both gifts and sacrifices for sins:

units.leftText: He is able to deal gently with those who are ignorant and misguided, since he himself is subject to weakness.
units.rightText: who can bear gently with the ignorant and erring, for that he himself also is compassed with infirmity;

units.leftText: That is why he is obligated to offer sacrifices for his own sins, as well as for the sins of the people.
units.rightText: and by reason thereof is bound, as for the people, so also for himself, to offer for sins.

units.leftText: No one takes this honor upon himself; he must be called by God, just as Aaron was.
units.rightText: And no man taketh the honor unto himself, but when he is called of God, even as was Aaron.

units.leftText: So also Christ did not take upon Himself the glory of becoming a high priest, but He was called by the One who said to Him: “You are My Son; today I have become Your Father.”
units.rightText: So Christ also glorified not himself to be made a high priest, but he that spake unto him, Thou art my Son, This day have I begotten thee:
leftNotes: 5:5 Psalm 2:7|PSA 2:7*; literally today I have begotten You

units.leftText: And in another passage God says: “You are a priest forever in the order of Melchizedek.”
units.rightText: as he saith also in another place, Thou art a priest for ever After the order of Melchizedek.

units.leftText: During the days of Jesus’ earthly life, He offered up prayers and petitions with loud cries and tears to the One who could save Him from death, and He was heard because of His reverence.
units.rightText: Who in the days of his flesh, having offered up prayers and supplications with strong crying and tears unto him that was able to save him from death, and having been heard for his godly fear,

units.leftText: Although He was a Son, He learned obedience from what He suffered.
units.rightText: though he was a Son, yet learned obedience by the things which he suffered;

units.leftText: And having been made perfect, He became the source of eternal salvation to all who obey Him
units.rightText: and having been made perfect, he became unto all them that obey him the author of eternal salvation;

units.leftText: and was designated by God as high priest in the order of Melchizedek. Milk and Solid Food (1 Corinthians 3:1–9|1CO 3:1-9*)
units.rightText: named of God a high priest after the order of Melchizedek.

units.leftText: We have much to say about this, but it is hard to explain, because you are dull of hearing.
units.rightText: Of whom we have many things to say, and hard of interpretation, seeing ye are become dull of hearing.

units.leftText: Although by this time you ought to be teachers, you need someone to reteach you the basic principles of God’s word. You need milk, not solid food!
units.rightText: For when by reason of the time ye ought to be teachers, ye have need again that some one teach you the rudiments of the first principles of the oracles of God; and are become such as have need of milk, and not of solid food.
leftNotes: 5:12 Or of the oracles of God

units.leftText: For everyone who lives on milk is still an infant, inexperienced in the message of righteousness.
units.rightText: For every one that partaketh of milk is without experience of the word of righteousness; for he is a babe.

units.leftText: But solid food is for the mature, who by constant use have trained their senses to distinguish good from evil.
units.rightText: But solid food is for fullgrown men, even those who by reason of use have their senses exercised to discern good and evil.

units.leftText: Therefore let us leave the elementary teachings about Christ and go on to maturity, not laying again the foundation of repentance from dead works, and of faith in God,
units.rightText: Wherefore leaving the doctrine of the first principles of Christ, let us press on unto perfection; not laying again a foundation of repentance from dead works, and of faith toward God,
leftNotes: 6:1 Or from acts that lead to death

units.leftText: instruction about baptisms, the laying on of hands, the resurrection of the dead, and eternal judgment.
units.rightText: of the teaching of baptisms, and of laying on of hands, and of resurrection of the dead, and of eternal judgment.

units.leftText: And this we will do, if God permits.
units.rightText: And this will we do, if God permit.

units.leftText: It is impossible for those who have once been enlightened, who have tasted the heavenly gift, who have shared in the Holy Spirit,
units.rightText: For as touching those who were once enlightened and tasted of the heavenly gift, and were made partakers of the Holy Spirit,

units.leftText: who have tasted the goodness of the word of God and the powers of the coming age —
units.rightText: and tasted the good word of God, and the powers of the age to come,

units.leftText: and then have fallen away — to be restored to repentance, because they themselves are crucifying the Son of God all over again and subjecting Him to open shame.
units.rightText: and then fell away, it is impossible to renew them again unto repentance; seeing they crucify to themselves the Son of God afresh, and put him to an open shame.

units.leftText: For land that drinks in the rain often falling on it and that produces a crop useful to those for whom it is tended receives the blessing of God.
units.rightText: For the land which hath drunk the rain that cometh oft upon it, and bringeth forth herbs meet for them for whose sake it is also tilled, receiveth blessing from God:

units.leftText: But land that produces thorns and thistles is worthless, and its curse is imminent. In the end it will be burned.
units.rightText: but if it beareth thorns and thistles, it is rejected and nigh unto a curse; whose end is to be burned.

units.leftText: Even though we speak like this, beloved, we are convinced of better things in your case— things that accompany salvation.
units.rightText: But, beloved, we are persuaded better things of you, and things that accompany salvation, though we thus speak:

units.leftText: For God is not unjust. He will not forget your work and the love you have shown for His name as you have ministered to the saints and continue to do so.
units.rightText: for God is not unrighteous to forget your work and the love which ye showed toward his name, in that ye ministered unto the saints, and still do minister.

units.leftText: We want each of you to show this same diligence to the very end, in order to make your hope sure.
units.rightText: And we desire that each one of you may show the same diligence unto the fulness of hope even to the end:

units.leftText: Then you will not be sluggish, but will imitate those who through faith and patience inherit what has been promised. God’s Unchangeable Promise
units.rightText: that ye be not sluggish, but imitators of them who through faith and patience inherit the promises.

units.leftText: When God made His promise to Abraham, since He had no one greater to swear by, He swore by Himself,
units.rightText: For when God made promise to Abraham, since he could swear by none greater, he sware by himself,

units.leftText: saying, “I will surely bless you and multiply your descendants.”
units.rightText: saying, Surely blessing I will bless thee, and multiplying I will multiply thee.

units.leftText: And so Abraham, after waiting patiently, obtained the promise.
units.rightText: And thus, having patiently endured, he obtained the promise.

units.leftText: Men swear by someone greater than themselves, and their oath serves as a confirmation to end all argument.
units.rightText: For men swear by the greater: and in every dispute of theirs the oath is final for confirmation.

units.leftText: So when God wanted to make the unchanging nature of His purpose very clear to the heirs of the promise, He guaranteed it with an oath.
units.rightText: Wherein God, being minded to show more abundantly unto the heirs of the promise the immutability of his counsel, interposed with an oath;

units.leftText: Thus by two unchangeable things in which it is impossible for God to lie, we who have fled to take hold of the hope set before us may be strongly encouraged.
units.rightText: that by two immutable things, in which it is impossible for God to lie, we may have a strong encouragement, who have fled for refuge to lay hold of the hope set before us:

units.leftText: We have this hope as an anchor for the soul, firm and secure. It enters the inner sanctuary behind the curtain,
units.rightText: which we have as an anchor of the soul, a hope both sure and stedfast and entering into that which is within the veil;

units.leftText: where Jesus our forerunner has entered on our behalf. He has become a high priest forever in the order of Melchizedek.
units.rightText: whither as a forerunner Jesus entered for us, having become a high priest for ever after the order of Melchizedek.

units.leftText: This Melchizedek was king of Salem and priest of God Most High. He met Abraham returning from the slaughter of the kings and blessed him,
units.rightText: For this Melchizedek, king of Salem, priest of God Most High, who met Abraham returning from the slaughter of the kings and blessed him,

units.leftText: and Abraham apportioned to him a tenth of everything. First, his name means “king of righteousness.” Then also, “king of Salem” means “king of peace.”
units.rightText: to whom also Abraham divided a tenth part of all (being first, by interpretation, King of righteousness, and then also King of Salem, which is, King of peace;

units.leftText: Without father or mother or genealogy, without beginning of days or end of life, like the Son of God, he remains a priest for all time.
units.rightText: without father, without mother, without genealogy, having neither beginning of days nor end of life, but made like unto the Son of God), abideth a priest continually.

units.leftText: Consider how great Melchizedek was: Even the patriarch Abraham gave him a tenth of the plunder.
units.rightText: Now consider how great this man was, unto whom Abraham, the patriarch, gave a tenth out of the chief spoils.

units.leftText: Now the law commands the sons of Levi who become priests to collect a tenth from the people — that is, from their brothers — though they too are descended from Abraham.
units.rightText: And they indeed of the sons of Levi that receive the priest’s office have commandment to take tithes of the people according to the law, that is, of their brethren, though these have come out of the loins of Abraham:

units.leftText: But Melchizedek, who did not trace his descent from Levi, collected a tenth from Abraham and blessed him who had the promises.
units.rightText: but he whose genealogy is not counted from them hath taken tithes of Abraham, and hath blessed him that hath the promises.

units.leftText: And indisputably, the lesser is blessed by the greater.
units.rightText: But without any dispute the less is blessed of the better.

units.leftText: In the case of the Levites, mortal men collect the tenth; but in the case of Melchizedek, it is affirmed that he lives on.
units.rightText: And here men that die receive tithes; but there one, of whom it is witnessed that he liveth.

units.leftText: And so to speak, Levi, who collects the tenth, paid the tenth through Abraham.
units.rightText: And, so to say, through Abraham even Levi, who receiveth tithes, hath paid tithes;

units.leftText: For when Melchizedek met Abraham, Levi was still in the loin of his ancestor. A Superior Priesthood
units.rightText: for he was yet in the loins of his father, when Melchizedek met him.

units.leftText: Now if perfection could have been attained through the Levitical priesthood ( for on this basis the people received the law), why was there still need for another priest to appear — one in the order of Melchizedek and not in the order of Aaron?
units.rightText: Now if there was perfection through the Levitical priesthood (for under it hath the people received the law), what further need was there that another priest should arise after the order of Melchizedek, and not be reckoned after the order of Aaron?

units.leftText: For when the priesthood is changed, the law must be changed as well.
units.rightText: For the priesthood being changed, there is made of necessity a change also of the law.

units.leftText: He of whom these things are said belonged to a different tribe, from which no one has ever served at the altar.
units.rightText: For he of whom these things are said belongeth to another tribe, from which no man hath given attendance at the altar.

units.rightText: But now they desire a better country, that is, a heavenly: wherefore God is not ashamed of them, to be called their God; for he hath prepared for them a city.

units.leftText: By faith Abraham, when he was tested, offered up Isaac on the altar. He who had received the promises was ready to offer his one and only son,
units.rightText: By faith Abraham, being tried, offered up Isaac: yea, he that had gladly received the promises was offering up his only begotten son;
leftNotes: 11:17 Or only begotten son or unique son

units.leftText: even though God had said to him, “Through Isaac your offspring will be reckoned.”
units.rightText: even he to whom it was said, In Isaac shall thy seed be called:

units.leftText: Abraham reasoned that God could raise the dead, and in a sense, he did receive Isaac back from death. The Faith of Isaac, Jacob, and Joseph (Genesis 27–50*)
units.rightText: accounting that God is able to raise up, even from the dead; from whence he did also in a figure receive him back.

units.leftText: By faith Isaac blessed Jacob and Esau concerning the future.
units.rightText: By faith Isaac blessed Jacob and Esau, even concerning things to come.

units.leftText: By faith Jacob, when he was dying, blessed each of Joseph’s sons and worshiped as he leaned on the top of his staff.
units.rightText: By faith Jacob, when he was dying, blessed each of the sons of Joseph; and worshipped, leaning upon the top of his staff.

units.leftText: By faith Joseph, when his end was near, spoke about the exodus of the Israelites and gave instructions about his bones. The Faith of Moses (Exodus 2–15*; Acts 7:20–22|ACT 7:20-22*)
units.rightText: By faith Joseph, when his end was nigh, made mention of the departure of the children of Israel; and gave commandment concerning his bones.

units.leftText: By faith Moses’ parents hid him for three months after his birth, because they saw that he was a beautiful child, and they were unafraid of the king’s edict.
units.rightText: By faith Moses, when he was born, was hid three months by his parents, because they saw he was a goodly child; and they were not afraid of the king’s commandment.

units.leftText: By faith Moses, when he was grown, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter.
units.rightText: By faith Moses, when he was grown up, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter;

units.leftText: He chose to suffer oppression with God’s people rather than to experience the fleeting enjoyment of sin.
units.rightText: choosing rather to share ill treatment with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season;

units.leftText: He valued disgrace for Christ above the treasures of Egypt, for he was looking ahead to his reward.
units.rightText: accounting the reproach of Christ greater riches than the treasures of Egypt: for he looked unto the recompense of reward.

units.leftText: By faith Moses left Egypt, not fearing the king’s anger; he persevered because he saw Him who is invisible.
units.rightText: By faith he forsook Egypt, not fearing the wrath of the king: for he endured, as seeing him who is invisible.

units.leftText: By faith he kept the Passover and the sprinkling of blood, so that the destroyer of the firstborn would not touch Israel’s own firstborn.
units.rightText: By faith he kept the passover, and the sprinkling of the blood, that the destroyer of the firstborn should not touch them.

units.leftText: By faith the people passed through the Red Sea as on dry land; but when the Egyptians tried to follow, they were drowned. The Faith of Many (Joshua–Malachi*)
units.rightText: By faith they passed through the Red sea as by dry land: which the Egyptians assaying to do were swallowed up.

units.leftText: By faith the walls of Jericho fell, after the people had marched around them for seven days.
units.rightText: By faith the walls of Jericho fell down, after they had been compassed about for seven days.

units.leftText: By faith the prostitute Rahab, because she welcomed the spies in peace, did not perish with those who were disobedient.
units.rightText: By faith Rahab the harlot perished not with them that were disobedient, having received the spies with peace.

units.leftText: And what more shall I say? Time will not allow me to tell of Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, David, Samuel, and the prophets,
units.rightText: And what shall I more say? for the time will fail me if I tell of Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah; of David and Samuel and the prophets:

units.leftText: who through faith conquered kingdoms, administered justice, and gained what was promised; who shut the mouths of lions,
units.rightText: who through faith subdued kingdoms, wrought righteousness, obtained promises, stopped the mouths of lions,

units.leftText: quenched the raging fire, and escaped the edge of the sword; who gained strength from weakness, became mighty in battle, and put foreign armies to flight.
units.rightText: quenched the power of fire, escaped the edge of the sword, from weakness were made strong, waxed mighty in war, turned to flight armies of aliens.

units.leftText: Women received back their dead, raised to life again. Others were tortured and refused their release, so that they might gain a better resurrection.
units.rightText: Women received their dead by a resurrection: and others were tortured, not accepting their deliverance; that they might obtain a better resurrection:

units.leftText: Still others endured mocking and flogging, and even chains and imprisonment.
units.rightText: and others had trial of mockings and scourgings, yea, moreover of bonds and imprisonment:

units.leftText: They were stoned, they were sawed in two, they were put to death by the sword. They went around in sheepskins and goatskins, destitute, oppressed, and mistreated.
units.rightText: they were stoned, they were sawn asunder, they were tempted, they were slain with the sword: they went about in sheepskins, in goatskins; being destitute, afflicted, ill-treated
leftNotes: 11:37 NE, WH, BYZ, and TR include they were put to the test,

units.leftText: The world was not worthy of them. They wandered in deserts and mountains, and hid in caves and holes in the ground.
units.rightText: (of whom the world was not worthy), wandering in deserts and mountains and caves, and the holes of the earth.

units.leftText: These were all commended for their faith, yet they did not receive what was promised.
units.rightText: And these all, having had witness borne to them through their faith, received not the promise,

units.leftText: God had planned something better for us, so that together with us they would be made perfect.
units.rightText: God having provided some better thing concerning us, that apart from us they should not be made perfect.

units.leftText: Therefore, since we are surrounded by such a great cloud of witnesses, let us throw off every encumbrance and the sin that so easily entangles, and let us run with endurance the race set out for us.
units.rightText: Therefore let us also, seeing we are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us,

units.leftText: Let us fix our eyes on Jesus, the author and perfecter of our faith, who for the joy set before Him endured the cross, scorning its shame, and sat down at the right hand of the throne of God.
units.rightText: looking unto Jesus the author and perfecter of our faith, who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising shame, and hath sat down at the right hand of the throne of God.

units.leftText: Consider Him who endured such hostility from sinners, so that you will not grow weary and lose heart. God Disciplines His Sons
units.rightText: For consider him that hath endured such gainsaying of sinners against himself, that ye wax not weary, fainting in your souls.

units.leftText: In your struggle against sin, you have not yet resisted to the point of shedding your blood.
units.rightText: Ye have not yet resisted unto blood, striving against sin:

units.leftText: And you have forgotten the exhortation that addresses you as sons: “My son, do not take lightly the discipline of the Lord, and do not lose heart when He rebukes you.
units.rightText: and ye have forgotten the exhortation which reasoneth with you as with sons, My son, regard not lightly the chastening of the Lord, Nor faint when thou art reproved of him;

units.leftText: For the Lord disciplines the one He loves, and He chastises every son He receives.”
units.rightText: For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, And scourgeth every son whom he receiveth.
leftNotes: 12:6 Literally and He flogs every son He receives; Proverbs 3:11–12|PRO 3:11-12* (see also LXX)

units.leftText: Endure suffering as discipline; God is treating you as sons. For what son is not disciplined by his father?
units.rightText: It is for chastening that ye endure; God dealeth with you as with sons; for what son is there whom his father chasteneth not?

units.leftText: If you do not experience discipline like everyone else, then you are illegitimate children and not true sons.
units.rightText: But if ye are without chastening, whereof all have been made partakers, then are ye bastards, and not sons.

units.leftText: Furthermore, we have all had earthly fathers who disciplined us, and we respected them. Should we not much more submit to the Father of our spirits and live?
units.rightText: Furthermore, we had the fathers of our flesh to chasten us, and we gave them reverence: shall we not much rather be in subjection unto the Father of spirits, and live?

units.leftText: Our fathers disciplined us for a short time as they thought best, but God disciplines us for our good, so that we may share in His holiness.
units.rightText: For they indeed for a few days chastened us as seemed good to them; but he for our profit, that we may be partakers of his holiness.

units.leftText: No discipline seems enjoyable at the time, but painful. Later on, however, it yields a harvest of righteousness and peace to those who have been trained by it.
units.rightText: All chastening seemeth for the present to be not joyous but grievous; yet afterward it yieldeth peaceable fruit unto them that have been exercised thereby, even the fruit of righteousness.
leftNotes: 12:11 Or it yields the peaceful fruit of righteousness

units.leftText: Therefore strengthen your limp hands and weak knees.
units.rightText: Wherefore lift up the hands that hang down, and the palsied knees;

units.leftText: Make straight paths for your feet, so that the lame may not be disabled, but rather healed. A Call to Holiness (1 Peter 1:13–21|1PE 1:13-21*)
units.rightText: and make straight paths for your feet, that that which is lame be not turned out of the way, but rather be healed.

units.leftText: Pursue peace with everyone, as well as holiness, without which no one will see the Lord.
units.rightText: Follow after peace with all men, and the sanctification without which no man shall see the Lord:

units.leftText: See to it that no one falls short of the grace of God, and that no root of bitterness springs up to cause trouble and defile many.
units.rightText: looking carefully lest there be any man that falleth short of the grace of God; lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you, and thereby the many be defiled;

units.leftText: See to it that no one is sexually immoral, or is godless like Esau, who for a single meal sold his birthright.
units.rightText: lest there be any fornicator, or profane person, as Esau, who for one mess of meat sold his own birthright.

units.leftText: For you know that afterward, when he wanted to inherit the blessing, he was rejected. He could find no ground for repentance, though he sought the blessing with tears. An Unshakable Kingdom (Exodus 20:18–21|EXO 20:18-21*; Deuteronomy 5:22–33|DEU 5:22-33*)
units.rightText: For ye know that even when he afterward desired to inherit the blessing, he was rejected; for he found no place for a change of mind in his father, though he sought it diligently with tears.

units.leftText: For you have not come to a mountain that can be touched and that is burning with fire; to darkness, gloom, and storm;
units.rightText: For ye are not come unto a mount that might be touched, and that burned with fire, and unto blackness, and darkness, and tempest,
leftNotes: 12:18 Literally to what can be touched and

units.leftText: to a trumpet blast or to a voice that made its hearers beg that no further word be spoken.
units.rightText: and the sound of a trumpet, and the voice of words; which voice they that heard entreated that no word more should be spoken unto them;

units.leftText: For they could not bear what was commanded: “If even an animal touches the mountain, it must be stoned.”
units.rightText: for they could not endure that which was enjoined, If even a beast touch the mountain, it shall be stoned;

units.leftText: The sight was so terrifying that even Moses said, “I am trembling with fear.”
units.rightText: and so fearful was the appearance, that Moses said, I exceedingly fear and quake:

units.leftText: Instead, you have come to Mount Zion, to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem. You have come to myriads of angels
units.rightText: but ye are come unto mount Zion, and unto the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and to innumerable hosts of angels,

units.leftText: in joyful assembly, to the congregation of the firstborn, enrolled in heaven. You have come to God the Judge of all, to the spirits of the righteous made perfect,
units.rightText: to the general assembly and church of the firstborn who are enrolled in heaven, and to God the Judge of all, and to the spirits of just men made perfect,

units.leftText: to Jesus the mediator of a new covenant, and to the sprinkled blood that speaks a better word than the blood of Abel.
units.rightText: and to Jesus the mediator of a new covenant, and to the blood of sprinkling that speaketh better than that of Abel.

units.leftText: See to it that you do not refuse Him who speaks. For if the people did not escape when they refused Him who warned them on earth, how much less will we escape if we reject Him who warns us from heaven?
units.rightText: See that ye refuse not him that speaketh. For if they escaped not when they refused him that warned them on earth, much more shall not we escape who turn away from him that warneth from heaven:

units.leftText: At that time His voice shook the earth, but now He has promised, “Once more I will shake not only the earth, but heaven as well.”
units.rightText: whose voice then shook the earth: but now he hath promised, saying, Yet once more will I make to tremble not the earth only, but also the heaven.

units.leftText: The words “Once more” signify the removal of what can be shaken — that is, created things — so that the unshakable may remain.
units.rightText: And this word, Yet once more, signifieth the removing of those things that are shaken, as of things that have been made, that those things which are not shaken may remain.

units.leftText: Therefore, since we are receiving an unshakable kingdom, let us be filled with gratitude, and so worship God acceptably with reverence and awe.
units.rightText: Wherefore, receiving a kingdom that cannot be shaken, let us have grace, whereby we may offer service well-pleasing to God with reverence and awe:

units.leftText: “For our God is a consuming fire.”
units.rightText: for our God is a consuming fire.

units.leftText: Continue in brotherly love.
units.rightText: Let love of the brethren continue.

units.leftText: Do not neglect to show hospitality to strangers, for by so doing some people have entertained angels without knowing it.
units.rightText: Forget not to show love unto strangers: for thereby some have entertained angels unawares.

units.leftText: Remember those in prison as if you were bound with them, and those who are mistreated as if you were suffering with them.
units.rightText: Remember them that are in bonds, as bound with them; them that are ill-treated, as being yourselves also in the body.

units.leftText: Marriage should be honored by all and the marriage bed kept undefiled, for God will judge the sexually immoral and adulterers. Christ’s Unchanging Nature
units.rightText: Let marriage be had in honor among all, and let the bed be undefiled: for fornicators and adulterers God will judge.

units.leftText: Keep your lives free from the love of money and be content with what you have, for God has said: “Never will I leave you, never will I forsake you.”
units.rightText: Be ye free from the love of money; content with such things as ye have: for himself hath said, I will in no wise fail thee, neither will I in any wise forsake thee.

units.leftText: So we say with confidence: “The Lord is my helper; I will not be afraid. What can man do to me?”
units.rightText: So that with good courage we say, The Lord is my helper; I will not fear: What shall man do unto me?

units.leftText: Remember your leaders who spoke the word of God to you. Consider the outcome of their way of life and imitate their faith.
units.rightText: Remember them that had the rule over you, men that spake unto you the word of God; and considering the issue of their life, imitate their faith.

units.leftText: Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.
units.rightText: Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and to-day, yea and for ever.

units.leftText: Do not be carried away by all kinds of strange teachings, for it is good for the heart to be strengthened by grace and not by foods of no value to those devoted to them.
units.rightText: Be not carried away by divers and strange teachings: for it is good that the heart be established by grace; not by meats, wherein they that occupied themselves were not profited.

units.leftText: We have an altar from which those who serve at the tabernacle have no right to eat.
units.rightText: We have an altar, whereof they have no right to eat that serve the tabernacle.

units.leftText: Although the high priest brings the blood of animals into the Holy Place as a sacrifice for sin, the bodies are burned outside the camp.
units.rightText: For the bodies of those beasts whose blood is brought into the holy place by the high priest as an offering for sin, are burned without the camp.

units.leftText: And so Jesus also suffered outside the city gate, to sanctify the people by His own blood.
units.rightText: Wherefore Jesus also, that he might sanctify the people through his own blood, suffered without the gate.

units.leftText: Therefore let us go to Him outside the camp, bearing the disgrace He bore.
units.rightText: Let us therefore go forth unto him without the camp, bearing his reproach.

units.leftText: For here we do not have a permanent city, but we are looking for the city that is to come. Sacrifice, Obedience, and Prayer
units.rightText: For we have not here an abiding city, but we seek after the city which is to come.

units.leftText: Through Jesus, therefore, let us continually offer to God a sacrifice of praise, the fruit of lips that confess His name.
units.rightText: Through him then let us offer up a sacrifice of praise to God continually, that is, the fruit of lips which make confession to his name.

units.leftText: And do not neglect to do good and to share with others, for with such sacrifices God is pleased.
units.rightText: But to do good and to communicate forget not: for with such sacrifices God is well pleased.

units.leftText: Obey your leaders and submit to them, for they watch over your souls as those who must give an account. To this end, allow them to lead with joy and not with grief, for that would be of no advantage to you.
units.rightText: Obey them that have the rule over you, and submit to them: for they watch in behalf of your souls, as they that shall give account; that they may do this with joy, and not with grief: for this were unprofitable for you.

units.leftText: Pray for us; we are convinced that we have a clear conscience and desire to live honorably in every way.
units.rightText: Pray for us: for we are persuaded that we have a good conscience, desiring to live honorably in all things.

units.leftText: And I especially urge you to pray that I may be restored to you soon. Benediction and Farewell
units.rightText: And I exhort you the more exceedingly to do this, that I may be restored to you the sooner.

units.leftText: Now may the God of peace, who through the blood of the eternal covenant brought back from the dead our Lord Jesus, that great Shepherd of the sheep,
units.rightText: Now the God of peace, who brought again from the dead the great shepherd of the sheep with the blood of an eternal covenant, even our Lord Jesus,

units.leftText: equip you with every good thing to do His will. And may He accomplish in us what is pleasing in His sight through Jesus Christ, to whom be glory forever and ever. Amen.
units.rightText: make you perfect in every good thing to do his will, working in us that which is well-pleasing in his sight, through Jesus Christ; to whom be the glory for ever and ever. Amen.
leftNotes: 13:21 BYZ and TR every good work

units.leftText: I urge you, brothers, to bear with my word of exhortation, for I have only written to you briefly.
units.rightText: But I exhort you, brethren, bear with the word of exhortation: for I have written unto you in few words.

units.leftText: Be aware that our brother Timothy has been released. If he arrives soon, I will come with him to see you.
units.rightText: Know ye that our brother Timothy hath been set at liberty; with whom, if he come shortly, I will see you.

units.leftText: Greet all your leaders and all the saints. Those from Italy send you greetings.
units.rightText: Salute all them that have the rule over you, and all the saints. They of Italy salute you.

units.leftText: Grace be with all of you.
units.rightText: Grace be with you all. Amen.
